title: 3Sum
description: Given an integer array `nums`, return every distinct triplet `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` where `i`, `j`, `k` are all different indices and the three values sum to `0`. The result must not contain the same triplet twice. The order of triplets, and of numbers within a triplet, does not matter.

examples.explanation: No three values sum to zero.

hints: Trying all triples is O(n^3). If the array is sorted, fixing one number reduces the rest to a two-sum problem.
After sorting, fix nums[i] and use two pointers l = i+1, r = end to look for a pair summing to -nums[i].
Move l up if the sum is too small, r down if too large. After recording a hit, and for each fixed i, skip repeated values so no triplet repeats.
starterCode:
class Solution:
    def threeSum(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[List[int]]:

solution.explanation: Sort the array, then fix each element nums[i] as the smallest of the triplet and search the suffix after it with two pointers for a pair that sums to -nums[i]. A sum that is too small moves the left pointer right, too large moves the right pointer left. To avoid duplicates, skip an i equal to the previous value and, after a hit, advance past equal left values. Sorting is O(n log n) and the double loop is O(n^2), so time is O(n^2) with O(1) extra space beyond the output.
